questions.question: Q1. The wake requirement: the owner's rule is 'if I do not call Ari, it must not answer.' Find the mechanism that enforces this. Is it a wake word, a push-to-talk, a confidence threshold, or nothing? Can a spoken sentence that does not address ARIES cause an action? Trace the path.
questions.answer: It is a WAKE WORD, and it is purely lexical on the TRANSCRIPT — not a push-to-talk, not a confidence threshold, and not a separate wake-word model. The mechanism is real and it demonstrably holds for the FIRST utterance. But it is not sufficient to enforce the owner's rule, for two independent reasons: (1) after the name is heard ALONE, the next utterance in the room is submitted as a command with no second wake word, for up to 6 seconds; (2) the wake vocabulary includes `ара` (an everyday Macedonian interjection) and `harry`/`hari` (a common name), both as whole words, so a sentence addressed to a person can wake it. So YES: a spoken sentence that does not address ARIES can cause an action.

TRACED PATH. listen() (voice.py:245-303) -> decode_command() (:555-576) -> `if not text: continue` (:850-853) -> `command = wake_match(text)` (:854) -> `if command is None: pulse.emit(0.0, PHASE_IDLE); log('· not addressed ...'); continue` (:855-860). WHAT KIND OF GATE IT IS. `_WAKE_RE` (:340-342) is `^[\s.,!?\-—"'«»]*(<name>)[\s.,!?\-—:;"'«»]+(.*)$` with IGNORECASE|DOTALL: the name must be at the very start and be followed by at least one separator. There is NO push-to-talk anywhere in voice.py or the unit. There is NO confidence threshold on the wake decision: LANGUAGE_CONFIDENCE_MIN (:76) only decides whether a vocabulary prompt is passed to the decoder (:561), and the stricter-while-audio-plays thresholds were deliberately removed on 2026-10-03 with the measurements recorded in the file (:77-92). The generic Whisper hallucination thresholds (:73-75, applied :132-142) run BEFORE the wake gate and are about whether the segment is speech at all, not about whether it was addressed.

CORRECT REJECTIONS: 'Ariana Grande is my favourite' -> None; 'arithmetic is hard' -> None; 'So Ari, what do you think' -> None; 'THE PRIME MINISTER, Ari, said' -> None; 'аре ајде бе' -> None; 'I said to Harry: open the terminal' -> None; 'ara, delete everything' -> None (Latin 'ara' is NOT a wake token; only Cyrillic 'ара' is); 'open YouTube' -> None; 'Hey Siri, play music' -> None. EXECUTED PROBE, FALSE WAKES THAT DO FIRE: 'ара, што правиш' -> 'што правиш'; 'Harry, close the door' -> 'close the door'; 'Hari, install vscode' -> 'install vscode'; 'Ary - delete file /tmp/x' -> 'delete file /tmp/x'. The file's own comment at :336-339 states the design intent ('a false wake is worse than a missed one here, because a false wake executes something') — these two tokens violate that intent.

THE FOLLOW-UP WINDOW IS THE LARGER HOLE. voice.py:861-887: when wake_match returns the empty string (the name alone), serve() logs '· woken — listening for the command', calls listen() again with --follow-silence-ms 900 and --follow-timeout 6.0, and submits whatever comes back. Inside that 6-second window the wake requirement is SUSPENDED for everything the microphone hears — the television, a phone call, the other person in the room. WHAT THE GATE DOES ACHIEVE, measured: 641 '· not addressed' lines across the whole journal and 68 in the current 2.5-hour boot, with zero actions in the current boot, against continuous loudspeaker speech reaching the microphone. The gate is the single load-bearing control and it is carrying real traffic.

questions.question: Q2. Self-triggering: ARIES speaks through the same machine it listens on. What prevents its own speech from being transcribed as a command? A playback-suppression mechanism was measured and REMOVED (false wakes 2->2, real commands over music 7/10->5/10). What, if anything, replaced it?
questions.answer: Six things replaced it, and the primary one is structural rather than statistical: ARIES no longer records from the output sink's monitor, and it never records while its own text-to-speech is playing. Those two are sound. The content-based echo check that the file presents as the replacement for the removed threshold is, in the normal flow, largely INERT, because it is conditioned on audio actually playing and ARIES's own speech is blocking and finishes before the next capture starts. And nothing content-based covers audio ARIES itself STARTED but did not synthesise (a song), which was the exact 2026-09-29 vector; that case is now caught only by the server-side runaway guard, i.e. by pattern after the fact, not by content before.
questions.source: experiments/voice/voice.py:77-92 (the removal and its measurements), :386-512 (capture-source resolution: _pw_nodes, real_sources, default_source_name, source_is_connected, capture_target), :93 and :515-534 (_LAST_SPOKEN, echoes_own_speech, speak_and_remember), :345-383 (audio_is_playing + 2 s cache), :560 and :573-575 (where the echo check is applied), :59-67 and :144-147 (prompt hygiene and prompt-echo rejection), :545-552 (caption_hallucination), :534 and :915-917 (blocking speech is deliberate); aries/workspace/runaway.py:1-19 and :53-80; aries/api/routes.py:1149, 1158; aries/speech/__init__.py:52-56 and :107-121 (speaking()/stop()); aries/workspace/capabilities.py:898-904 (the `say` capability's own TTS path)
questions.detail:
WHAT REPLACED IT, in order of how much weight each carries.

1. CAPTURE-SOURCE RESOLUTION (the real fix, and the file says so at :90-92). real_sources() (:418-426) accepts a node only if media.class == 'Audio/Source' AND '.monitor' not in node.name; capture_target() (:479-512) prefers default.audio.source when it is a real source, otherwise the first real source, otherwise None, and prints the reason once per change. EXECUTED PROOF: the live pw-record (PID 128822) targets `alsa_input.usb-046d_081d_EE25F9C0-00.mono-fallback`, which pw-dump shows as Audio/Source state=running, and the daemon logged `· input: microphone '...mono-fallback'` — the branch that means default.audio.source and the chosen source agree. No monitor is in the path. This removes the 34 dB advantage documented at :394-398.

2. SERIALISATION. serve() handles one utterance at a time, and every spoken reply goes through speak_and_remember() -> speech.speak(..., blocking=True) (:534), with the rationale written at :915-917 ('speaking while the microphone is open means transcribing ourselves. That loop actually happened, 44 times'). listen() starts pw-record and terminates it per utterance (:263, :287-292), so while ARIES's own TTS plays there is NO capture process. This is the mechanism that actually prevents TTS self-capture.

3. CONTENT-BASED ECHO REJECTION — present, but largely inert where it matters. echoes_own_speech() (:515-523) rejects a transcript when >=60% of its words longer than 2 characters appear in _LAST_SPOKEN[0]. EXECUTED PROBE: echoes_own_speech('Дискот е на 8.5 проценти', same) -> True; echoes_own_speech('Ari, play some music', 'Playing Bona and Lozano') -> False. GAPS, by source inspection: (a) it is applied ONLY when audio_is_playing() is true (:573), and because speak() is blocking the player has already exited by the time the next decode_command() runs, so audio_is_playing() (whose cache is 2 s, :363) will normally be False and the check never runs; (b) it compares against exactly ONE sentence, _LAST_SPOKEN[0]; (c) _LAST_SPOKEN is only ever written by speak_and_remember() (:533), which wraps only the daemon's own replies.

4. PROMPT HYGIENE. PROMPTS (:64-67) are bare word lists in both languages and deliberately contain no 'Ari, <command>' sentence, with the 2026-09-29 regurgitation incident recorded at :59-63. transcribe() additionally drops a transcript whose every word is a prompt word (:144-147).

5. caption_hallucination() (:545-552) drops standalone caption echoes. EXECUTED PROBE: 'Thank you for watching' -> True, 'Thanks for watching!' -> True, but 'Subtitles by the Amara.org community' -> False and 'Thank you.' -> False. The Amara string is the SINGLE MOST FREQUENT hallucination in the live journal (it appears ~10 times in the current boot alone) and the regex misses it because it requires exactly 'subtitles by amara org'. Harmless today (it is rejected by the wake gate), but the filter does not do what the journal shows it needs to do.

6. THE SERVER-SIDE PATTERN BACKSTOP. aries/workspace/runaway.py, called at routes.py:1149 before any goal is created. Its module docstring (:1-19) is a verbatim account of the 2026-09-29 loop and states the design principle: 'Every individual command looked legitimate; only the PATTERN was wrong.' For source 'voice': 3 identical requests in 120 s, or more than 6 requests in 60 s, pauses the source for 600 s (:28-32, :67-80) and returns 429 (routes.py:1158). This, not any content check, is what now bounds a music-driven loop.

REMAINING SELF-TRIGGERING SURFACE (source inspection, NOT executed).
(a) Audio ARIES started but did not synthesise. play_music / open_url / browser_open put a song on the loudspeakers; _LAST_SPOKEN never sees it, so echoes_own_speech cannot recognise it. The acoustic coupling is REAL and proven: the live journal is full of transcribed loudspeaker content. The only things between a hallucinated wake word out of music and an action are the wake gate and the runaway guard.
(b) A SECOND TTS PATH exists that bypasses _LAST_SPOKEN entirely. The `say` capability at aries/workspace/capabilities.py:898-904 calls speech.speak(args['text'], blocking=True) inside the aries-core process, with no update to the daemon's _LAST_SPOKEN and no coordination with the microphone loop. Because the goal executes asynchronously in aries-core while voice.py's await_outcome gives up after --reply-wait 8.0 s (voice.py:903, :946-947), a `say` that fires later than that plays while pw-record is live. Grep confirms there are exactly two speech.speak call sites outside the module: voice.py's speak_and_remember and this one. Its own comment at capabilities.py:902-903 asserts 'The voice daemon uses the non-blocking form instead' — that is STALE: voice.py:534 passes blocking=True.
(c) speech.speaking() IS DOCUMENTED AS THE GATE AND IS NEVER CALLED. aries/speech/__init__.py:55 says "`speaking()` exists to be gated on, and `stop()` exists so that a person who starts talking cuts ARIES off mid-word". EXECUTED GREP across aries/, experiments/ and scripts/: speaking() has ZERO call sites, and stop() has one — inside speak() itself (:271). Neither the barge-in behaviour nor the 'do not transcribe while speaking' interlock the docstring promises exists in code.

questions.question: Q3. Language forcing: the service runs with `--languages mk,en`. What happens to an utterance in a third language? Is it rejected, mistranscribed, or forced into one of the two?
questions.answer: FORCED into whichever of mk and en scores higher, and then mistranscribed. It is never rejected for being a third language. The code path that would reject an unsupported language is unreachable under this configuration. The only consequence of a near-zero winner is that the vocabulary prompt is withheld; the transcript is still produced and still handed to the wake gate. Separately: the `--languages mk,en` in the unit OVERRIDES aries.flags.listen_languages(), which on this machine returns ('en',) alone — so the unit reintroduces exactly the mk/en misdetection that flag was created to remove.
questions.source: experiments/voice/voice.py:98-120 (pick_language), :555-568 (decode_command, including the unreachable rejection), :73-76 (thresholds), :561 (prompt withheld below LANGUAGE_CONFIDENCE_MIN=0.10), :974-987 (the flags fallback and the condition under which it runs); systemd/aries-voice.service:31-35 (the hardcoded --languages mk,en and its stated reasoning); aries/flags.py:177-204 (primary_language, listen_languages)
questions.detail:
MECHANISM. pick_language() (:107-120) calls model.detect_language(audio), keeps only the allowed codes (`ranked = [(l, p) for l, p in all_probs if l in allowed]`), and returns `max(ranked, key=lambda lp: lp[1])`. faster-whisper's detect_language returns probabilities for ALL languages in all_language_probs, so with allowed=('mk','en') `ranked` is never empty: the `return None, 0.0` at :110 is unreachable, and so is the only rejection branch in the whole path. decode_command() :563-568 reads `if language is None: ... if args.languages and language not in args.languages: DROPPED.append('unsupported detected language'); text = ''` — that block requires language to be None, which pick_language cannot produce here. Under `--languages mk,en` it is DEAD CODE. A German, Serbian or Turkish sentence is therefore decoded as Macedonian or English, whichever won between the two, at any absolute probability.

WHAT IS LEFT. Only (a) `prompt = PROMPTS.get(language) if probability >= LANGUAGE_CONFIDENCE_MIN else None` (:561, threshold 0.10 at :76) — a weak winner forfeits the vocabulary prompt, which the file argues is the right trade at :111-118; (b) the generic hallucination thresholds no_speech<=0.6 / avg_logprob>=-1.0 / compression<=2.4 (:73-75, applied :132-142); and then (c) the wake gate. So a third-language utterance can only cause an ACTION if the forced decode happens to produce something that starts with a wake token.

EXECUTED PROOF from the live journal that the forcing really happens and really goes through at near-zero confidence: `· not addressed [mk 0.06] (1085ms): 'Рубен, што ја даде, не даде дочекар, не даде престаја, што ја дисплефи'`, `· not addressed [mk 0.21] (1206ms): 'Сеќавање на Министерството за Доброј Доброј Доброј'`, and English-forced lines at [en 0.01], [en 0.02], [en 0.04], [en 0.05], [en 0.08], [en 0.09]. Every one of those was kept, transcribed and handed to the wake gate; none was dropped for language.

SECOND FINDING IN THIS ANSWER. voice.py's own --languages help text (:948) says to omit the flag so that `aries.flags.listen_languages()` decides, 'which is the single place that decides'. aries/flags.py:194-204 returns ('en',) when the primary language is English — and the comment there records WHY (2026-10-03: unconstrained detection answered Macedonian speech with pt/bg/ro/hr/pl and the filter then discarded 7 of 10 real commands; 'One language cannot be misdetected'). But voice.py:975 only consults flags `if not args.languages and not args.language`, and systemd/aries-voice.service:35 hardcodes `--languages mk,en`. So the running service bypasses the single source of truth and keeps two languages in play. The [mk 0.06] and [mk 0.21] lines in the live journal are that bypass in action.

questions.question: Q4. What is the actual end-to-end path from a transcribed string to a submitted goal? Does spoken input go through the same router, planner, policy and verification as typed input, or does it have a shortcut anywhere?
questions.answer: No privilege shortcut. Spoken input reaches exactly the same submit function, planner, capability policy and verification recorder as a typed command-bar goal, and no policy function in the path even receives the origin. I looked specifically for a privileged desktop route and did not find one. There are, however, three real ASYMMETRIES, and one of them is a safety-relevant loss: spoken input has no interpretation-confirmation step and, because it is submitted with present=False, an approval freeze produces no window at all.

TYPED PATH, for comparison. POST /api/aries/command (routes.py:1053-1108) resolves intents and, when the goal is not an exact navigate/screen match, INSERTS a 'Do: <text>' row whose action is `{kind: run_automation, automation_id: 'aries.workspace.submit', text}` (:1081-1083). The user picks it, the shell POSTs it to /shell/act, and routes.py:1147 lands in the identical branch. Same submit, same plan, same policy, same verification.

(a) Spoken input NEVER calls /api/aries/command, so aries.shell.intents.resolve never runs for it. Every spoken sentence becomes a workspace goal. Different route, not more authority. act()'s docstring (voice.py:786-792) states this deliberately.
(b) NO INTERPRETATION CONFIRMATION. A typed user sees the candidate list and chooses the 'Do: ...' row; the transcript is submitted the instant the wake gate passes. The one surface where a typed user can catch a misunderstanding before it executes has no spoken equivalent. Note that _tell_voice_outcome only NOTIFIES — it does not speak; I checked, because a second TTS path there would have been a self-triggering vector.

questions.question: Q5. Can a transcription error cause a MUTATING capability to run without approval? Trace whether spoken input can reach a non-read effect, and what gates it.
questions.answer: YES — on the DETERMINISTIC branch, and by design. The system's stated rule is at aries/operator/service.py:303: 'A guess is proposed; an exact match is performed.' A transcript that fullmatches one of the hardcoded command patterns is treated as an exact match and executes with no approval. The only approval allowlist on that branch is capabilities.SENSITIVE, nine names. Three mutators — media_control, set_volume and set_brightness — escape even the operator.enabled check and the hourly action budget, because they return before the block that applies them. The MODEL branch is properly gated: unrecognised speech becomes an agent_task goal and every non-read effect freezes at `proposed`, because operator.confirm_model_plans is live TRUE.

  service.py:561  `if step["capability"] in capabilities.SENSITIVE and not step.get("approved") ...` -> approvals.propose, state='proposed'. SENSITIVE (capabilities.py:71) is exactly nine names: trash_file, install_app, move_file, browser_fill, ui_action, wifi_connect, service_control, clipboard_write, type_text.
  service.py:568  `if step.get("from_model") and not step.get("approved") and operator.confirm_model_plans` -> state='proposed'. `from_model` is set at EXACTLY ONE place, capabilities.py:1283, inside the model-plan validator. A recognize() match never carries it, so this gate never fires for deterministic speech.
Everything else executes. Non-SENSITIVE mutating capabilities reachable from the spoken vocabulary: open_app, open_url, search_web, play_music, create_file, create_folder, open_path, python_project, build_python, browser_open, browser_follow, browser_close, media_control, set_volume, set_brightness, remember, refresh_news, brief, health.

RESIDUAL GATES ON BRANCH A, and the three capabilities that escape them.
  For `kind in WRITES` (capabilities.py:72-74): capabilities.py:1033-1035 refuses unless operator.enabled, then :1036 _arm() applies operator.max_actions_per_hour. LIVE: operator.enabled = true (executed GET /api/aries/operator and read-only sqlite row id 19); max_actions_per_hour absent from the DB, so the default 60.
  For open_app / open_url / search_web / refresh_news / brief / health: capabilities.py:1067-1070 -> operator.run, which checks cfg['enabled'] (operator/service.py:296-301) and then :303-309 — proposes only `if made.source == "model"`. desktop_plan() returns Plan(source="router") (capabilities.py:375, :391), so a router-sourced plan PERFORMS.
  media_control (capabilities.py:693-708), set_volume (:710-745) and set_brightness (:873-896) RETURN BEFORE line 1028. They are in neither WRITES nor the :1067 set, so they get NO operator.enabled check, NO hourly budget and NO approval. The only things in front of them are the wake gate and the runaway guard. The patterns that reach them are short and bare: a lone 'pause', 'stop', 'next', 'play', 'resume', 'mute', 'unmute', 'namali', 'намали', 'turn down', 'lower', 'turn up', 'raise', 'dim', or 'volume <n>' (capabilities.py:198-205, :232-239). media_control's final fallback is 'playpause' (:700), so any matched verb acts.

BRANCH B — MODEL, PROPERLY GATED. When recognize() declines (or the clause check at service.py:64-66 fires), plan() returns an agent_task step (service.py:35 or :65-66) and the m14 agent runs. agent.py:357 calls registry.policy, which for a non-read effect requires operator.enabled (registry.py:101-102) and then returns False if `cap.requires_approval and not approved` (:123-124) or if `not approved and operator.confirm_model_plans` (:125-126). LIVE: confirm_model_plans = true (executed GET /api/aries/operator; the key is absent from aries_settings so it is at its code default True). So on this machine EVERY non-read effect on the model branch freezes at `proposed`. That is the strong gate, and the asymmetry is the finding: the branch driven by a language model is gated, and the branch driven by a regex on a Whisper transcript is not.

WHAT IS PROVEN AND WHAT IS NOT. PROVEN by executed journal read: mistranscribed text IS submitted as a goal and acted on (2026-09-24T22:39:41 `✓ 'split to YouTube.' — Task queued`; 22:40:04 `✓ 'опен YouTube пемплеј да сонг 2 бона е еднот Лозано.' — Task queued`; 80 actions over the journal's life). PROVEN by executed probe: the wake gate passes 'Ari create folder /home/stamenovmartin/x' -> 'create folder /home/stamenovmartin/x' and 'Ari: trash file ~/notes.txt' -> 'trash file ~/notes.txt'. NOT PROVEN by execution: that a real mistranscription has in fact landed on one of the non-SENSITIVE mutating patterns and executed. Demonstrating that would require speaking to the system, which this review was forbidden to do. The claim above is a source-traced reachability result, not a measured incident.

SECONDARY NOTE. checked_path() (capabilities.py:393-415) does bound file writes: inside $HOME, never $HOME itself, no symlinked parents, no dot-directories. Its own comment at :407-414 records that ARIES's own source tree is NOT excluded, so a new file can appear inside the package unapproved — 'a hole in the fence rather than the lock'. That applies to create_file/create_folder, which are reachable from speech without approval.

questions.question: Q6. Is there any bound on how often voice can submit goals (a rate limit, a runaway guard)?
questions.answer: YES, and it is the single best-designed control in this path. aries/workspace/runaway.py enforces a repeat limit, a rate limit and a trip-and-pause, with STRICTER numbers for source 'voice' than for typed input, and it is checked before any goal row is created. Three weaknesses: the state is in-process memory so an aries-core restart resets it; the resume endpoint needs no approval and the API on this machine accepts unauthenticated requests as the owner; and the bucket key comes from the request body.
questions.source: aries/workspace/runaway.py:1-19 (the 2026-09-29 incident this exists for), :28-32 (the constants), :53-80 (check), :83-88 (resume), :91-94 (status); aries/api/routes.py:1118 (the client-supplied `source`), :1121-1132 (the guard endpoints), :1149-1158 (the check and the 429); experiments/voice/voice.py:671-675 (the daemon speaks the 429), :807-823 and :745-782 (serial loop, bounded PendingReplies), :534 and :915-917 (blocking speech paces the loop); aries/workspace/service.py:21 (MAX_CONCURRENT=3), :146-148 (20-goal queue cap); aries/operator/settings.py:41 (max_actions_per_hour 60)
questions.evidence_kind: source inspection + executed read-only API probe
questions.detail:
THE GUARD. runaway.check(text, source) at routes.py:1149, before service.submit. For source 'voice': REPEAT_LIMIT 3 identical normalised requests inside REPEAT_WINDOW_S 120 (runaway.py:29, :67, :71-72) and RATE_LIMIT 6 inside RATE_WINDOW_S 60 (:31, :68-69, :73-74). Typed input gets 6 and 15. Either trip sets _paused_until[source] = now + PAUSE_S 600 and clears the deque (:77-80); the request returns HTTP 429 (routes.py:1158) and, on the tripping request only, emits a WARNING notification keyed `runaway.voice` (:1152-1157). A later request inside the pause returns 429 with the remaining seconds (:58-59). voice.py translates the 429 into a spoken sentence in both languages (:673-675), so the person hears why it stopped. EXECUTED: GET /api/aries/shell/guard -> HTTP 200 `{"paused":{}}` — nothing is paused now.

CLIENT-SIDE PACING (not a limit, but it bounds the rate in practice). serve() (voice.py:820-923) is strictly serial: one listen(), one decode, one act(), one blocking reply. speak_and_remember uses blocking=True (:534) with the rationale at :915-917. await_outcome waits up to --reply-wait 8.0 s (:903, :946). PendingReplies holds at most 16 goals (:750-751), polls at most 2 per cycle with a 0.3 s timeout each (:763, :771), and persists only IDs, language and expiry — never transcripts (:724-728).

OTHER BOUNDS IN THE PATH. 20 active goals max (service.py:146-148); MAX_CONCURRENT = 3 (service.py:21); operator.max_actions_per_hour = 60 for `kind in WRITES` via _arm (capabilities.py:1036) — but, as Q5 records, media_control/set_volume/set_brightness never reach that block; request text bounded to 2000 characters (service.py:97, routes.py:1048); plan clause cap of 6 (service.py:37-38).

WEAKNESSES.
(a) STATE IS IN-PROCESS MEMORY (runaway.py:18-19, :34-36). The module argues a restart is 'itself a reasonable reset', but a crash-restart loop in aries-core would also clear a legitimate pause. The pause is NOT durable and NOT visible after a restart.
(b) THE RESUME ENDPOINT IS UNGATED IN PRACTICE. POST /api/aries/shell/guard/resume?source=voice (routes.py:1128-1132) calls runaway.resume with no approval and no audit entry. permissions.py maps /api/aries/shell/act to EXECUTE but /api/aries/shell to {GET: VIEW_DATA, '*': MANAGE_TOOLS}; because API_KEY is empty, main.py:103-104 grants every unauthenticated caller shared_key_owner, which satisfies both. EXECUTED CONFIRMATION of the open API: an unauthenticated GET returned 200.
(c) THE BUCKET KEY IS CLIENT-SUPPLIED. `source` is a field on ShellActionRequest (routes.py:1118) and defaults to 'default' (routes.py:1149), so anything that can reach 127.0.0.1:8000 can choose the laxer bucket. The voice daemon always sends 'voice' (voice.py:795); nothing verifies it.

findings.title: The bare-name follow-up window suspends the wake requirement for 6 seconds
findings.what: When wake_match() returns the empty string (the name alone), serve() re-opens the microphone with --follow-timeout 6.0 and submits whatever it captures, explicitly 'with no second wake word' (:866). Inside that window the owner's rule — 'if I do not call Ari, it must not answer' — does not hold for anything the microphone hears: the television, a phone call, the other person in the room.
findings.evidence: Source :861-887. EXECUTED journal read (older build, same structure): 2026-09-24T22:39:39 `· woken with no command: 'Ari.'` then 22:39:41 `✓ 'split to YouTube.' — Task queued (heard in 763ms, acted in 30ms)`; 22:39:56 `· woken with no command: 'Ari.'` then 22:40:04 `✓ 'опен YouTube пемплеј да сонг 2 бона е еднот Лозано.' — Task queued`.
findings.why_it_matters: This is the only place in the path where the gate the whole design rests on is switched off, and it is switched off by a single mis-heard syllable. The reason given (:862-866) is sound product reasoning — people do pause after a wake word — but the window is unconditional and unverified: nothing checks that the follower is the same speaker, the same direction, or even plausibly a command.
findings.suggested_direction: Narrow it rather than remove it: require the follow-up to be recognisable as a command (a recognize() match or a verb-initial sentence) before submitting it, shorten the window, or require the wake word again when the follow-up does not parse.

findings.title: `ара` and `harry` are whole-word wake tokens; both are things people say to people
findings.what: `ара` is an everyday Macedonian colloquial interjection and `harry`/`hari` is a common name. Both are listed as wake tokens, so a sentence addressed to a person wakes ARIES and its remainder is submitted as a goal.
findings.evidence: EXECUTED probe of the real module: 'ара, што правиш' -> 'што правиш'; 'Harry, close the door' -> 'close the door'; 'Hari, install vscode' -> 'install vscode'.
findings.why_it_matters: The file's own comment at :336-339 states the governing principle: 'a false wake is worse than a missed one here, because a false wake executes something.' These two entries contradict it. The mishearings they were added for ('Хари', 'Hari' from a leading H) are real, but `ара` in particular buys very little and costs a whole class of room conversation.
findings.suggested_direction: Drop `ара` and consider requiring a following comma or an imperative for `harry`/`hari`; measure the missed-wake cost before and after rather than assuming it.

findings.title: Deterministic transcripts execute mutating capabilities with no approval; the allowlist is nine names and three mutators escape even the operator gate
findings.what: A transcript that re.fullmatches a hardcoded pattern is treated as an exact match and performed ('A guess is proposed; an exact match is performed', operator/service.py:303). The only approval allowlist on that branch is capabilities.SENSITIVE (9 names). media_control, set_volume and set_brightness return before capabilities.py:1028, so they get no operator.enabled check, no operator.max_actions_per_hour budget and no approval — only the wake gate and the runaway guard.
findings.evidence: Source trace as cited. LIVE settings (executed GET /api/aries/operator and read-only sqlite): operator.enabled=true, confirm_model_plans=true, max_actions_per_hour absent (default 60). EXECUTED journal read proves mistranscribed text does reach submit and act (80 actions across the journal; two verbatim examples in VOICE-01). NOT executed: a mistranscription actually landing on a mutating pattern.
findings.why_it_matters: The gating asymmetry is backwards relative to input reliability. The model branch — where a model interpreted the text — freezes every non-read effect for approval. The deterministic branch — where a Whisper transcript of possibly-loudspeaker audio matched a regex — performs. Whisper's output is not an exact match in the sense that phrase means for typed input, and the journal shows exactly how garbled it can be.
findings.suggested_direction: Make the approval decision a function of the EFFECT, not of which matcher produced the step, and name voice as a distinct origin so that `origin == 'voice'` can require approval for a non-read effect independently of operator.confirm_model_plans. At minimum, route media_control/set_volume/set_brightness through the operator.enabled check and the hourly budget.

findings.title: The echo guard that is presented as the replacement for the removed suppression is inert in the normal flow
findings.what: echoes_own_speech() is applied only when audio_is_playing() is true (:573). Because speak() is blocking (:534) and the player has exited before the next listen() begins, audio_is_playing() will normally be False at the next decode, so the check does not run. It also compares against exactly one sentence, _LAST_SPOKEN[0], which is written only by speak_and_remember() (:533).
findings.evidence: Source inspection. The removal note at :90-92 says 'Echo rejection against our own last sentence stays, because it identifies the one case by content rather than by confidence' — the mechanism stays, but its precondition is normally false. EXECUTED probe confirms the function itself works: echoes_own_speech('Дискот е на 8.5 проценти', same) -> True.
findings.why_it_matters: What actually prevents TTS self-capture is the serialisation (no pw-record while speaking) and the capture-source choice, not this check. The documentation attributes the protection to the wrong mechanism, which matters because the serialisation is the thing a future change (non-blocking replies, a second listener) would silently break.
findings.suggested_direction: Either drop the audio_is_playing() precondition and keep a short ring buffer of the last few spoken sentences, or restate in the file that serialisation is the real guard so nobody removes it believing the echo check covers it.

findings.title: Nothing content-based covers audio ARIES started but did not synthesise — the exact 2026-09-29 vector
findings.what: _LAST_SPOKEN only ever holds ARIES's own TTS. A song started by play_music/open_url/browser_open is not in it, so echoes_own_speech cannot recognise a wake word hallucinated out of that song. The protections for that case are structural (not recording from the sink monitor) and statistical (the runaway guard), not content-based.
findings.evidence: Source inspection. The acoustic coupling is EXECUTED-PROVEN: the current boot's journal is full of transcribed loudspeaker content ('Thanks for watching!', 'Subtitles by the Amara.org community', motivational-video speech), all of it reaching the wake gate.
findings.why_it_matters: This was the incident that produced 44 goals in 20 minutes. The two things that fixed it are real and well-argued, but neither acts on content, so the wake gate is the only pre-action filter for the loudest noise source in the room.
findings.suggested_direction: If ARIES knows it started playback for a goal, that is a fact available to the daemon; consider making the goal's media title part of the echo-rejection vocabulary for as long as it plays.

findings.title: The service unit overrides aries.flags.listen_languages(), reinstating the mk/en misdetection the flag was created to remove
findings.where: systemd/aries-voice.service:31-35; experiments/voice/voice.py:974-987 and the --languages help text at :948; aries/flags.py:194-204
findings.what: voice.py consults aries.flags only when neither --languages nor --language was given, and its own help text calls flags 'the single place that decides'. The unit hardcodes `--languages mk,en`. aries/flags.py:194-204 returns ('en',) alone when the primary language is English, precisely because 'One language cannot be misdetected'.
findings.evidence: Source inspection plus EXECUTED journal read: `· not addressed [mk 0.06] (1085ms): 'Рубен, што ја даде...'` and `[mk 0.21] ... 'Сеќавање на Министерството за Доброј Доброј Доброј'` — Macedonian decodes at near-zero language confidence on a machine whose language policy says to listen in English only.
findings.why_it_matters: Two files document opposite decisions, both with measurements, and the unit wins silently. Whichever is right, the configuration should have ONE source, and right now the one that the code calls the single source of truth is the one being bypassed.
findings.suggested_direction: Remove --languages from the unit and let flags decide, or change flags and record why the unit's choice supersedes the 2026-10-03 measurement.

findings.title: speech.speaking() is documented as the interlock and has zero callers; the `say` capability is a second TTS path that bypasses the echo memory
findings.what: The module docstring states that speaking() 'exists to be gated on' and that stop() exists so a person can cut ARIES off mid-word. An executed grep across aries/, experiments/ and scripts/ finds ZERO callers of speaking() and exactly one caller of stop() — inside speak() itself. Separately, the `say` capability calls speech.speak(..., blocking=True) from the aries-core process with no update to voice.py's _LAST_SPOKEN and no coordination with the microphone loop; its own comment at :902-903 ('The voice daemon uses the non-blocking form instead') contradicts voice.py:534, which passes blocking=True.
findings.evidence: EXECUTED grep: the only speech.speak call sites outside aries/speech/ are experiments/voice/voice.py:534 and aries/workspace/capabilities.py:904. No speaking() call site anywhere.
findings.why_it_matters: Two promised behaviours do not exist (barge-in, and a speak/listen interlock), and one real path can put synthesised speech on the loudspeakers at a moment the daemon has no record of. Because goals execute asynchronously and voice.py gives up waiting after --reply-wait 8.0 s, a late `say` can play while pw-record is live.
findings.suggested_direction: Either implement the interlock the docstring describes, or delete the claim. Route the `say` capability's text back to the daemon's echo memory, or have it decline while the daemon holds the microphone.

findings.title: caption_hallucination misses the most frequent real hallucination on this machine
findings.what: The regex requires the normalised text to be exactly 'subtitles by amara org'. The live journal's actual string is 'Subtitles by the Amara.org community', which normalises to 'subtitles by the amara org community' and does not fullmatch.
findings.evidence: EXECUTED probe: caption_hallucination('Subtitles by the Amara.org community') -> False; caption_hallucination('Thanks for watching!') -> True. EXECUTED journal count: the Amara string appears ~10 times in the current 2.5-hour boot and dozens of times overall, always as '· not addressed' rather than '· dropped'.
findings.why_it_matters: Harmless today, because the wake gate rejects it. But the filter exists to keep known caption echoes out of the transcript stream, and the one echo this machine actually produces is not in it — which means the filter was written from the reference list rather than from this machine's journal.
findings.suggested_direction: Build the pattern from the live journal's own '· not addressed' and '· dropped' lines; the data is already there.

findings.title: The third-language rejection branch is unreachable under the running configuration
findings.what: pick_language() can only return None when `ranked` is empty, which cannot happen because detect_language returns probabilities for all languages and mk/en are always among them. The 'unsupported detected language' drop at :567 is therefore dead code under --languages mk,en.
findings.evidence: Source inspection of pick_language and decode_command; corroborated by the journal, which contains no 'unsupported detected language' line in 1372 lines while containing many near-zero-confidence decodes.
findings.why_it_matters: A reader of this file would reasonably conclude that an out-of-vocabulary language is rejected. It is not — it is forced into mk or en at any confidence. The deliberate trade is argued at :111-118 and I think it is the right trade; the dead branch is what makes the behaviour hard to see.
findings.suggested_direction: Delete the unreachable branch or make the forcing explicit in a log line, so the journal shows when a decode was a forced choice rather than a confident one.

findings.title: Spoken input has no interpretation-confirmation step, and an approval freeze opens no window
findings.where: aries/api/routes.py:1081-1083 (the typed confirmation) vs voice.py:890 (immediate submit); routes.py:1163 (present=not voice); aries/speech/replies.py:73, :207-208
findings.what: A typed user picks the 'Do: <text>' row from the command-bar candidate list before anything runs. A spoken transcript is submitted the instant the wake gate passes. And because voice submits with present=False, a goal frozen at `proposed` produces no dashboard window — the person's only signal is the spoken HELD line and a notification.
findings.evidence: Source trace. EXECUTED journal read shows garbled transcripts being submitted unconfirmed: `✓ 'опен YouTube пемплеј да сонг 2 бона е еднот Лозано.' — Task queued`.
findings.why_it_matters: The surface with the LEAST reliable input has the FEWEST confirmation steps. present=False is correct product reasoning (a window per sentence is what the owner asked not to have), but it also removes the place an approval would be seen.
findings.suggested_direction: For a non-read effect from voice, read the interpretation back before acting ('open YouTube — yes?'), which also covers VOICE-03; and make a `proposed` voice goal surface somewhere persistent, not only in a spoken sentence the person may miss.

findings.title: The runaway guard's state is non-durable and its resume is ungated on an open API
findings.what: The pause lives in process memory, so an aries-core restart clears it. POST /api/aries/shell/guard/resume takes a `source` and needs no approval and writes no audit row. And `source` itself is a client-supplied body field, so a caller can choose the laxer 'default' bucket.
findings.evidence: Source inspection. EXECUTED: the API accepts unauthenticated requests (API_KEY empty in .env; GET /api/aries/shell/guard returned HTTP 200 with no key), so the EXECUTE/MANAGE_TOOLS requirements in aries/api/permissions.py are satisfied by shared_key_owner for any local caller.
findings.why_it_matters: The guard is the main bound on a runaway voice loop and the thing that caught the 2026-09-29 incident in design. Its three weaknesses are each small, but together they mean a pause can be lost or lifted without a trace.
findings.suggested_direction: Persist the pause, audit resume, and derive the bucket from the authenticated principal or the route rather than from the body.

refuted_hypotheses.hypothesis: There is no microphone on this machine; ARIES is hearing the output sink's monitor.
refuted_hypotheses.verdict: REFUTED (this was an earlier reviewer's error and the task statement already corrected it; I verified it independently)
refuted_hypotheses.evidence: EXECUTED pw-dump: Audio/Source `alsa_input.usb-046d_081d_EE25F9C0-00.mono-fallback` state=running (USB 046d:081d). EXECUTED pw-metadata: default.audio.source is that same node. EXECUTED pgrep: PID 128822 `pw-record ... --target alsa_input.usb-046d_081d_EE25F9C0-00.mono-fallback -`. The daemon logged `· input: microphone 'alsa_input.usb-046d_081d_EE25F9C0-00.mono-fallback'`, which is capture_target()'s `wanted == chosen` branch (voice.py:507-508) — not the 'default source is not a microphone' branch and not the 'nothing is plugged in' branch. No '.monitor' node is in the path. The 68 transcriptions in the current boot are further proof the input carries signal.

refuted_hypotheses.hypothesis: The wake gate fires on prefixes, so 'Ariana', 'arithmetic' or a mid-sentence 'Ari' would wake it.
refuted_hypotheses.evidence: EXECUTED probe of the real _WAKE_RE: 'Ariana Grande is my favourite' -> None, 'arithmetic is hard' -> None, 'So Ari, what do you think' -> None, 'THE PRIME MINISTER, Ari, said' -> None, 'I said to Harry: open the terminal' -> None. The ^-anchor plus the required separator class holds.

refuted_hypotheses.hypothesis: Latin-script 'ara' is a wake token, so 'ara, delete everything' would wake it.
refuted_hypotheses.evidence: EXECUTED probe: wake_match('ara, delete everything') -> None. WAKE contains Cyrillic 'ара' only (voice.py:334). The Cyrillic form DOES fire (see VOICE-02) — the refutation is specifically about the Latin spelling.

refuted_hypotheses.hypothesis: Voice has a privileged or shortcut route into ARIES that typed input does not have.
refuted_hypotheses.evidence: voice.py:890 is the only call to act(), which posts kind='workspace' to /api/aries/shell/act. routes.py:1147 handles that in the SAME branch as the `aries.workspace.submit` action that /command hands the typed command bar (routes.py:1081-1083). Both reach service.submit, plan(), the same capability gates and the same record_verification (service.py:601-602). registry.policy (registry.py:96) and capabilities.execute take no actor or origin. An executed grep for 'voice' across aries/ found only five origin branches, and the only authority-relevant one makes voice STRICTER (runaway.py:29-31: 3/120s and 6/60s versus 6 and 15).

refuted_hypotheses.hypothesis: _tell_voice_outcome is a second text-to-speech path inside aries-core and could therefore self-trigger.
refuted_hypotheses.evidence: aries/workspace/service.py:385-399: it calls notify.emit() and db.commit(), nothing else. It creates a notification record; it does not speak. An executed grep confirms notifications never reach aries.speech.

refuted_hypotheses.hypothesis: Notifications are spoken, giving ARIES an unbounded way to put words on the loudspeakers.
refuted_hypotheses.evidence: EXECUTED grep for `speech.` across aries/ excluding aries/speech/: four hits, of which only aries/workspace/capabilities.py:904 calls speak(). The others are replies.sentence (contracts.py:149) and speech.available (introspection.py:126). No notification path speaks.

refuted_hypotheses.hypothesis: The removal of the playback-suppression thresholds left nothing in its place.
refuted_hypotheses.evidence: Six mechanisms replaced it, listed in full under Q2: capture-source resolution (voice.py:418-426, :479-512), serialisation with blocking speech (:534, :915-917), content-based echo rejection (:515-523, :573), prompt hygiene and prompt-echo rejection (:59-67, :144-147), caption_hallucination (:545-552), and the server-side runaway guard (runaway.py, routes.py:1149). Two of the six are sound; three have the gaps recorded in VOICE-04, VOICE-05 and VOICE-08. The removal itself is documented with its own measurements at voice.py:77-92 and I found no reason to disagree with it.

refuted_hypotheses.hypothesis: voice.py applies a confidence threshold to the wake decision, so a low-confidence utterance cannot act.
refuted_hypotheses.evidence: LANGUAGE_CONFIDENCE_MIN (voice.py:76) is used at exactly one place, :561, to decide whether to pass a vocabulary prompt. The wake decision (:854) is purely lexical. The per-segment thresholds at :73-75 run before the gate and concern whether the segment is speech at all. EXECUTED journal read shows transcripts kept and gated at language probability 0.01-0.06.

refuted_hypotheses.hypothesis: `--languages mk,en` means a third-language utterance is rejected as an unsupported language.
refuted_hypotheses.evidence: The rejection at voice.py:563-568 requires language to be None, and pick_language cannot return None when mk and en are both in `allowed` (detect_language returns all 99 probabilities, so `ranked` is non-empty). The branch is unreachable; a third language is forced into mk or en. No 'unsupported detected language' line appears anywhere in 1372 journal lines.

refuted_hypotheses.hypothesis: operator.confirm_model_plans has been turned off on this machine, so the model branch would execute mutations unapproved.
refuted_hypotheses.evidence: EXECUTED read-only GET /api/aries/operator -> confirm_model_plans: true. EXECUTED read-only sqlite (mode=ro) of var/aries.db aries_settings: the key is ABSENT, so it sits at its code default True (aries/operator/settings.py:24). The model branch therefore freezes every non-read effect at `proposed` (registry.py:125-126). Note the fragility: this is one toggle, and VOICE-03 is about the branch that does not consult it at all.

blocked_checks.check: Speak a wake word followed by a mutating command and observe whether it executes without approval — the executed proof for Q5.
